01 / FOOD & LIFTINGin the daily rotation

Eatifyaka macros tracker

the protein goal
got out of hand.

A personal app for food, training, and weight trends. Built around the way I actually log a day—including late dinners and patchy internet. Midnight still isn’t the boss of dinner.

  • Food, lifting, and trends in one place
  • Meal maths that stays actual maths
  • Works offline, because life happens

The product decision: let the tracking fit the routine, including when a day ends.

02 / MONEYalso in the daily rotation

Hisaabحساب

where did my
money go, again?

I could remember to log an expense. Categorising it? Apparently a step too far. So I built something that lets me capture first and make sense of it later.

  • Quick capture, even offline
  • Shared expenses without the mental maths
  • AI suggestions I get to approve

The product decision: separate quick capture from organising, and keep AI suggestions under the user’s control.

THE PERSON CONNECTING THE DOTS

a few different eras.
same curiosity.

Lahore, Pakistan ↗

I’m Usman. I studied mechanical engineering at NUST from 2021 to 2025, picked up object-oriented programming and machine learning along the way, and followed that curiosity into computer vision.

These days, I work on computer vision and build applications of my own. That combination has me thinking about both the technical challenge and the person trying to get something done.

The apps here are ones I actually use. They tend to start when something annoys me enough on a weekday that I spend a weekend on it.

a few things that didn’t fit in the intro +

Languages: Punjabi, Urdu, and English; conversational Turkish and A1 German.

Further learning: Machine Learning Specialization (Stanford / Coursera), Supply Chain Management Specialization (Rutgers), and ISTQB CTFL 4.0.

The workbench: Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, CUDA, Docker, Unity, SolidWorks, COMSOL, and a willingness to learn the next tool.
